newsitem.title: USA: Fed refrains from open market operations.
newsitem.headline: Fed refrains from open market operations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve stayed out of the open market on Tuesday, primary dealers.
Analysts had anticipated the Fed adding reserves to the banking system through a round of overnight system repurchase agreements.

Fed funds were trading below the Fed's 5-1/2 percent target rate at 5-7/16 percent, and was cited as a reason the Fed didn't enter the market. Plus, analysts said, they may have overestimated the Fed's add need for the current period.

The add need is expected to rise in the second half of the maintenance period, beginning on Thursday, as corporate and estimated second quarter estimated tax receipts pour into the Treasury, thereby raising its balance and draining Fed reserves.
As such, analysts predict the Fed will add permanent reserves thorugh an outright purchase of bills, although the timing is up in the air.
